symptom: A synthetic inherited Array.prototype numeric-index setter at index 17 can intercept canonical array output[i] writes. Two otherwise valid evaluation protocols differing only in their eighteenth metric-family entry then hash to the same truncated canonical array and may be classified as IDEMPOTENT_NOOP instead of CONFLICT. This was reproduced with synthetic metadata only; no real evidence or production path was affected.
lesson: An own-descriptor read does not protect a canonical digest if the fresh output array is populated through ordinary numeric assignment. Inherited setters can discard a validated last element and alias distinct append-only records; this is the same array-output trust-boundary mechanism previously found in untrusted snapshots, now affecting the vault digest.
guardrail: When constructing canonical arrays, define every numeric index as an own enumerable data property with Object.defineProperty. Regression-test two valid synthetic protocols differing only at a high index under a reversible inherited setter, assert stable distinct digests and CONFLICT, and preserve the historical fixed digest vectors. This does not authorize scoring or production connection.
